result.markdown:
# Nationwide Latency and DNS Degradation Incident

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** core_degradation at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** high (Direct evidence of DNS timeout alarm and severe query success rate and resolution time deviations on CORE-DNS-01 matching the exact timeline of national latency spikes. Changes, maintenance, and external events were checked and ruled out.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-24 10:45 to 2026-09-24 12:00
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-24 10:52
- **Affected:** CORE-DNS-01, S-SAH-001, S-SAH-002, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-004, S-SUD-002

## Summary

Internal core DNS timeout rate spike and service degradation on CORE-DNS-01 causing nationwide latency and resolution delays.

Nationwide latency increase and download volume drop due to core DNS resolution degradation, lasting from 2026-09-24 10:45 until recovery at 2026-09-24 12:00.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-24 10:45: Earliest onset of national latency deviation and CORE-DNS-01 query success percentage drop below baseline. [T1, T2, T3, ALR-0035]
- 2026-09-24 10:52: Major alarm ALM-000525 (DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE) raised on CORE-DNS-01. [T7, T9, ALM-000525]
- 2026-09-24 11:30: Worst impact peak for national latency (37.4 ms), resolution time (88.7 ms), and query success drop (92.7%). [T2, T3, ANM-000354, ANM-000322]
- 2026-09-24 12:00: National KPIs and core resolution times recovered to baseline levels. [T2, T3]
- 2026-09-24 12:05: Major alarm ALM-000525 on CORE-DNS-01 cleared. [T7, T9, ALM-000525]

## Evidence

- National latency_ms spiked above baseline starting at 2026-09-24 10:45, peaking at 37.4 ms at 2026-09-24 11:30. [T2, ANM-000354]
- CORE-DNS-01 query_success_pct dropped and resolution_ms spiked starting at 2026-09-24 10:45, with resolution reaching 88.7 ms at 2026-09-24 11:30. [T3, ANM-000322]
- Major alarm ALM-000525 (DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE) occurred on CORE-DNS-01 from 2026-09-24 10:52 to 12:05. [T7, T9, ALM-000525]
- No changes or maintenance windows were scheduled or executed on CORE-DNS-01 and its parents during the incident window. [T4, T5, T6]
- No external events were reported across all regions during the window. [T8]

## Hypotheses

1. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. Severe degradation on CORE-DNS-01 matches the exact timing and nature of the nationwide latency complaints, supported by a major DNS timeout alarm and lack of external changes or maintenance. [T3, T7, ALM-000525]
2. **bad_change** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. Change management logs show zero changes on CORE-DNS-01 or its parents during the relevant timeframe. [T4, T5]
3. **planned_maintenance** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. Maintenance checks returned no scheduled maintenance windows on CORE-DNS-01 or its parents. [T6]

## Ruled out

- T4: Checked changes between 08:00 and 13:00 and found no configuration changes on CORE-DNS-01 or its parents.
- T6: Checked maintenance schedules and confirmed no active windows during the event.
- T8: Checked external events and confirmed no external regional disruptions occurred.

## Recommended actions

- Investigate internal root cause of the CORE-DNS-01 timeout rate spike during the 10:45 to 12:00 window.
- Review resource utilization and query loads on CORE-DNS-01 to prevent recurrence.
